title: Individual Beef Cottage Pies with Golden Potato Swirls
dek: Six crisp pastry-shell cottage pies hold a thick beef-and-vegetable gravy beneath piped, deeply golden mashed-potato swirls for a freezer-friendly family dinner.
image_alt: Individual beef cottage pie in a pastry shell topped with golden piped mashed-potato swirls
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
12 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes and chilled
1/2 cup ice water, plus 1 to 2 tbsp only if needed
2 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
1 medium yellow onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice (about 1 1/2 cups)
1 medium carrot, peeled and cut into 1/4-inch dice (about 3/4 cup)
1 celery stalk, cut into 1/4-inch dice (about 1/2 cup)
1 large egg beaten with 1 tsp water, for brushing

instructions.name: Cut in the butter and chill the pastry
instructions.text: Whisk 2 1/2 cups flour with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cut in the 12 tablespoons chilled butter until the largest pieces are pea-size. Stir in 1/2 cup ice water with a fork; add only enough extra water for the dough to hold when squeezed. Press into a disk, wrap and refrigerate for 20 minutes while you start the potatoes and filling.

instructions.name: Make a pipeable potato topping
instructions.text: Cover the potatoes with cold water by 1 inch in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce to a steady simmer and cook 15 to 18 minutes, until a knife slides through without resistance. Drain thoroughly, return to the hot pan for 1 minute to steam dry, then mash until smooth with the 4 tablespoons softened butter, warm milk, egg yolk and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Spoon into a piping bag fitted with a large star tip, or keep covered for spreading.

instructions.name: Brown the beef safely
instructions.text: Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium-high. Add the beef and spread it into an even layer. Cook 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until no raw patches remain and several spots checked with a clean instant-read thermometer reach 160°F. Transfer the beef to a bowl with a slotted spoon, leaving about 1 tablespoon fat in the skillet.

instructions.name: Build a thick vegetable gravy
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook 7 to 9 minutes until tender and lightly browned. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, Worcestershire, thyme, black pepper and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt for 1 minute. Sprinkle in the 1 tablespoon flour and stir for 30 seconds. Gradually add the broth, scraping the browned bits from the pan, then return the beef. Simmer 4 to 6 minutes until the gravy leaves a trail when a spoon crosses the skillet. Fold in the peas and spread the filling on a plate to cool for 10 minutes.

instructions.name: Line six individual pie tins
instructions.text: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the lower third. Set six 4-inch metal pie tins on a rimmed sheet pan and lightly grease them. Roll the chilled dough about 1/8 inch thick. Cut six 6-inch circles, rerolling scraps once, and ease one into each tin without stretching. Trim to a 1/2-inch overhang, fold the edge inward and crimp. Prick each base four times with a fork.

instructions.name: Fill and pipe the visible potato swirls
instructions.text: Divide the cooled beef mixture among the shells, using about 2/3 cup per pie and keeping it below the rim. Pipe broad overlapping potato swirls from the outside toward the center so the beef is completely covered, matching the finished photograph. If you are not piping, spoon the potatoes on and drag a fork through the surface for raised ridges. Brush the exposed pastry rims with beaten egg.

instructions.name: Bake until the pastry and potatoes are golden
instructions.text: Bake 28 to 32 minutes, rotating the sheet pan after 20 minutes, until the pastry edges are deep golden and the potato ridges are browned. Check the center of two pies without touching the metal tin; both should reach 165°F. If the crust needs more color, cover the potato centers loosely with small foil circles and bake 3 to 5 minutes longer.

instructions.name: Rest before unmolding
instructions.text: Cool the pies in their tins for 10 minutes so the gravy settles and the pastry firms. Run a thin offset spatula around each rim, lift carefully and serve one pie per person. The finished pies should show crisp pastry shells and distinct golden potato swirls rather than loose mashed potatoes or exposed filling.

why_it_works: Cooling the thickened beef filling before assembly protects the raw pastry from steam and prevents the potato topping from sinking into the gravy.
Yukon Gold potatoes mash smoothly with modest dairy, while an egg yolk helps the piped ridges hold their shape and brown in the oven.
A small amount of flour turns measured broth into a cohesive gravy that stays inside each shell when the pie is cut or lifted.
Baking the pies on a preheated lower oven rack directs strong heat toward the pastry bases while the exposed potato ridges color above.
Individual tins create more crisp pastry edge per serving and make cooling, freezing and reheating more predictable than one deep casserole.
swaps: Use 1 pound ground lamb for individual shepherd's pies, cooking it to 160°F and spooning off all but 1 tablespoon rendered fat before adding the vegetables.
Replace the homemade pastry with about 1 1/2 pounds refrigerated pie dough. Roll and cut six 6-inch circles; avoid puff pastry, which can lift the filling unevenly.
For a dairy-free topping, use unsweetened oat milk and a firm plant butter. Confirm the Worcestershire sauce and pastry ingredients meet your dietary needs.
Frozen mixed peas and carrots can replace the fresh carrot and peas: use 1 1/4 cups, stir them in after the gravy thickens and simmer only until hot.
A 12-cup standard muffin pan makes smaller party pies. Cut 4 1/2-inch pastry circles, divide the filling and potato among 12 wells and begin checking after 22 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate cooled pies in airtight containers within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days. Reheat uncovered on a sheet pan in a 350°F oven for 18 to 22 minutes, checking the center reaches 165°F. Freeze fully baked, cooled pies individually wrapped for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating. The raw assembled pies should not be frozen because the uncooked pastry can absorb moisture from the filling.
notes: Four-inch metal pie tins conduct heat more effectively than thick ceramic ramekins and are the closest match to the crisp, freestanding pastry shells in the photograph.
Measure the filling after it thickens. A loose gravy can seep into the pastry and make the pies difficult to unmold, even if the flavor is correct.
Do not overwork pastry scraps. Stack and roll them once; kneading makes the final shells tougher and prone to shrinking.
Keep the potato topping warm enough to pipe but not steaming. If it stiffens, knead the filled piping bag gently or mix in 1 tablespoon warm milk.
Calories and estimated cost are per individual pie; actual values vary with beef prices, pastry trimming and the amount of potato topping used.

faqs.q: Why is this called cottage pie instead of shepherd's pie?
faqs.a: Cottage pie traditionally uses beef, while shepherd's pie uses lamb. These individual pies keep the beef filling and mashed-potato top that define cottage pie, then add a crisp pastry shell to match the photographed Australian-style presentation.

faqs.q: Can I assemble the individual pies ahead of time?
faqs.a: Yes. Cook and cool the filling and potatoes, line the tins, assemble the pies and refrigerate them covered for up to 24 hours. Brush the pastry rims just before baking and add 5 to 8 minutes to the bake time, verifying the centers reach 165°F.

faqs.q: How do I keep the pastry bottoms from becoming soggy?
faqs.a: Reduce the gravy until a spoon leaves a visible trail, cool it before filling, keep each portion below the rim and bake on a metal sheet pan in the lower third of a fully heated 400°F oven. Ceramic dishes and warm, runny filling both slow bottom browning.
